channel.title: KAIT2EN Fedora - Blog
channel.description: Release notes, upstreaming reports and T2 debugging write-ups.

item.title: How we fixed PSR on T2 Macs
item.description: A macOS display trace revealed the sink-specific sequence needed to enable Panel Self Refresh, reduce idle power and reach package C10 on T2 Macs.

item.title: Thunderbolterella Swallowed the Whole Apple
item.description: The hunt for deep package C-states on the 15,1 MacBook Pro gets ugly

item.title: Enfant Terrible
item.description: Fedora rebuilt the initramfs, four T2 modules quietly disappeared and an encrypted MacBook was left with a passphrase prompt it could not type into.

item.title: The MacBookPro15,1 finally has hybrid graphics
item.description: The discrete GPU can finally sleep while Intel drives the display, saving roughly 12 watts without giving up PRIME offload or external monitors.

item.title: Where did the watts go?
item.description: Package C-states, PROCHOT and a forest of PCI devices turned power debugging into two new tools instead of another collection of shell commands.

item.title: More than a fan controller
item.description: The T2 SMC gave Linux a working clock, charge limiting, standard fan control and enough sensors to finally ask where the heat and power are coming from.

item.title: The Navi rabbit hole
item.description: Hybrid graphics on the 16-inch MacBook Pros can turn the dGPU off. Bringing it back reliably is where the hardware starts telling a much stranger story.

item.title: Three watts and a dead USB port
item.description: Runtime-suspending Thunderbolt saved real power on the MacBookPro15,1, until USB 3 hotplug stopped working and the apparently obvious patch fell apart.

item.title: The small things you touch every day
item.description: Keyboard light, display brightness and the Fn key are small features until they reset after every reboot or disappear after every suspend.

item.title: Making the speakers sound like speakers
item.description: Getting sound out of the speakers was only the first half. Making it usable without crackling, wrong routing or damaged speakers became its own project.

item.title: The resume that took a minute
item.description: Suspend worked, but every CPU took several seconds to return. The fix was not making CPU startup faster. It was waiting for the right moment.

item.title: KAIT2EN is through the door
item.description: This is a copy of the text I wrote on Reddit when I released KaiT2EN in July 2026
